placements.why: The envelope's content — an instrument's calibration state, verified against named reference plates — names an organizational category (calibration record-keeping) that nothing in the existing (empty) strata covers. This matches the org's own named taxonomy tier (Calibration) rather than fitting under Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates, none of which plausibly hold an instrument-verification log. Minted standalone per the NEW check: no existing strata or leaf is even close, and this tier requires no parent already minted.

placements.title: Calibration status is established by verification against a fixed reference standard
placements.frame: Does this expression report an instrument's calibration being checked against a named external reference, and does the verification hold across the full operating range?
placements.why: All three segments — narrative and structured field-label alike — converge on the same recurring subject: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration is not simply asserted but checked against the June reference plates, and that check is reported to hold across the observing band. This is a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding (new instruments, new reference sets, new verification runs), not a one-time fact — the 88.4 MHz figure and the June-plates check are evidence for this theme, not leaves themselves. No existing leaf exists to reuse (graph structure is empty), so minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
